description:
A program reads its command line with System.argv(), as in Elixir: a list of binaries holding every token after the source path, verbatim, without the program name. `--` is not special. fz2's own options come before the path. Applies to `fz2 run|interp <file> args...` and to the built executable's C main(argc, argv).

Design (approved page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.6.html): ExecCtx.argv, filled by each driver (JIT Runtime::with_argv, interpreter run_backend_main, AOT fz_aot_setup from C main). The runtime helper fz_system_argv reads it, behind lib/system.fz's System.argv/0. One leading-options scan replaces parse_global_args' whole-line scan and parse_source_options' unknown-arg refusal; arguments are read with args_os. Fixtures gain an args: header key, passed to run, interp, the built binary and the elixir oracle.
title: System.argv/0 on all three paths
